brief.question: Which documented agent execution capabilities can support a complete product workflow, and what evidence is needed to release it?
brief.decision: Choose an execution boundary and evaluate accepted customer outcomes, recovery, authority and full cost.
brief.contribution: Three linked dossiers compare execution layers, inspect coding harnesses and reconcile current benchmark/productivity corrections.
brief.strongest_objection: Provider documentation and engineering guidance do not demonstrate product reliability or net productivity on a customer workload.

limitations: No original framework comparison, benchmark or customer-workload experiment was executed.
Source inspection and independent AI-worker review do not satisfy production named-human attestation.
This is a directed review of selected current interfaces and empirical corrections, not an exhaustive census or formal systematic review.
contrary_search: Read the February and July OpenAI benchmark audit sequence, including the retracted SWE-Bench Pro recommendation.
Separate the early-2025 METR RCT, the compromised later experiment, and the 2026 self-report survey.
Inspect provider availability, data-handling, checkpoint and side-effect boundaries.
coverage_gaps: Account-specific feature access and plan costs were not tested.
Human acceptance of the proposed product evaluation contract remains pending.

limitations: Results depend on task split and agent environment. This ledger records benchmark definition, not a live model ranking.

sources.title: Introducing SWE-bench Verified
limitations: Human filtering improves task feasibility but does not prove complete test coverage or absence of later training contamination.

sources.title: Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities
limitations: 138 audited tasks were selected from problems o3 did not consistently solve; 59.4% is not a random-sample estimate for all 500 tasks. Audit is OpenAI-reported; contamination examples do not establish every model/task is contaminated.

sources.title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
limitations: Publisher is a model provider. Automated screening plus review of flagged tasks can miss flaws outside the flagged subset; the ~30% number is an audit estimate, not a universal property of coding tasks.

sources.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
limitations: 16 developers with established repository expertise; 246 tasks in mature open-source projects; primarily Cursor with early-2025 Claude models. Total implementation time was self-reported, including review. Does not estimate all developers or October 2026 tools.

sources.title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
limitations: Selection of developers and tasks, changed pay, incomplete AI-disallowed tasks and concurrent work compromise current causal interpretation. Both later-study confidence intervals include zero.

sources.title: Measuring the Self-Reported Impact of Early-2026 AI on Technical Worker Productivity
limitations: Self-reported counterfactuals; convenience sample; low approximately 2% emailed response rate; nonrepresentative recruitment. Internal consistency does not verify real causal productivity gains.

sources.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
limitations: Network-dependent tasks and maximum action budget can alter comparability. Original 2024 baseline results describe historical models, not current capability.

sources.title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
limitations: Question-answer evaluation does not measure write actions such as posting, uploads or booking. Web facts can change. Language/cultural diversity and human annotation costs limit coverage.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
limitations: Simulated users and simplified retail/airline policies. Matching the final database/output can still miss intermediate policy violations. Original model results are historical.

sources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
limitations: Eight heterogeneous text-based environments; aggregate score combines different tasks/metrics. Historical 29-model experiment does not rank current tools.

sources.title: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
limitations: 108 tasks are diagnostic, not representative of all professions. Scores depend on release, action settings, task mix and stochastic behavior; paper HTML content/abstract-version model details should be reconciled before quoting a live ranking.

sources.title: ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?
limitations: Complete behavioral equivalence against compiled programs is narrower than open-ended product usefulness. Tests are finite; open-source programs may have been seen in training. Partial test percentage must not be relabeled fully resolved.
